sources_considered.why: Primary record establishes the award and the recognized AlphaFold work.
Original paper describes the architecture, domain constraints, database searches and end-to-end approach.
The earlier computational-chemistry award concerns combined classical and quantum methods; the announcement does not establish an earlier neural-symbolic system.
The later discussion is coauthored by Marcus, so it cannot independently establish that his claim was right.
The retrieved news page exposes only introductory text before subscription options and does not settle neurosymbolic classification.

evidence_items.locator: Press release, explanation of the Hassabis–Jumper half of the award
evidence_items.explanation: The official announcement connects the award to AlphaFold2 and protein structure prediction. It does not classify the system as neurosymbolic or establish priority within that category.

evidence_items.locator: Author contributions; architecture and Methods sections
evidence_items.explanation: The original paper describes an end-to-end neural approach incorporating physical and biological constraints, with sequence-search inputs and structural relaxation. Those features require interpretation before they can establish Marcus's neurosymbolic label; end-to-end training does not itself exclude that label.

unresolved_gaps: The sources do not settle whether AlphaFold's particular non-neural components constitute symbolic AI under the claim's intended definition.
No complete historical comparison using that same definition was established.
The formal award's omission of the term 'neurosymbolic' cannot by itself contradict the claim.
